name: VEML6035 low-lux ambient light sensor
description: Vishay 16-bit low-power, high-sensitivity ambient light sensor with a human-eye-like response, resolving down to 0.0004 lx/count and reading up to about 6.7 klx over I2C (ALS and WHITE channels, programmable gain, sensitivity and integration time). Chip runs on 1.7–3.6 V; the board is 3.3 V only. Sold as: MikroElektronika Ambient 11 Click (MIKROE-3990), a mikroBUS board with two 8-pin headers (AN, RST, CS, SCK, MISO, MOSI, 3V3, GND / PWM, INT, RX, TX, SCL, SDA, 5V, GND; only 3V3, GND, SCL, SDA and INT are connected), 2.2 k I2C pull-ups and fixed I2C address 0x29.
eli5: Tells your board how bright the light is, in lux, and is sensitive enough to measure a very dim room.

buildNotes: 3.3 V only: the board has no regulator and its 5V pin is not connected; the chip's absolute maximum is 4 V. Power it from 3V3.
The Click has two 8-pin mikroBUS headers; only 3V3, GND, SCL, SDA and (optionally) INT are used. Wire those with jumper leads.
Fixed I2C address 0x29. There is no ID register, so check for the device with i2c.scan().
Registers are 16 bits, sent and read LSB first. ALS_CONF (0x00) powers up as 0x0001 (shut down): write it with SD = 0, then wait one integration time before reading ALS counts from 0x04.

Lux = counts x resolution, resolution = 0.0004 x (800/IT) x (2 if DG=0) x (2 if GAIN=0) x (8 if SENS=1). The driver's default (GAIN=0, DG=0, SENS=1, 100 ms) gives 0.1024 lx/count, up to about 6711 lx.
For very dim light switch to SENS=0 and longer IT (down to 0.0004 lx/count at GAIN=1, DG=1, 800 ms, max about 26 lx).
The WHITE channel (0x05) only updates when CHANNEL_EN (bit 2) is set; the driver sets it by default.
The board's power LED can light the sensor; shade it for dark-room readings.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from veml6035 import VEML6035

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
# GAIN=0, DG=0, SENS=1, 100 ms: 0.1024 lx per count, up to about 6711 lx
sensor = VEML6035(i2c, gain=0, dg=0, sens=1, it_ms=100)
while True:
    print('Lux=%.1f White=%d' % (sensor.lux(), sensor.white()))
    time.sleep(1)
